Becki Ripley Pinckard
 
·
17w
This was my list that I compiled from AI and asking the group as well…
How many deep plane facelifts do you perform each year? How many so you do each day?
* Is deep plane your primary facelift technique?
* Am I actually a good candidate for a deep plane lift, or would another procedure be better?
* Can I see before-and-after photos of patients around my age with similar facial features? And long term?
What improvements can I realistically expect in my:
* Neck
* Jawline
* Jowls
* Midface
* What won’t this surgery improve?
* How long should my results last?
* Will I still look like myself?
Do you perform a true deep plane facelift or a SMAS facelift?
* Will you also tighten the platysma muscles in my neck?
* Will you remove excess fat under my chin if needed?
* Will you address deep neck structures (digastric muscles or submandibular glands) if they’re contributing to fullness?
* Will you use drains?
* Where will my incisions be?
Additional procedures
Ask whether you would benefit from combining surgery with:
* Upper or lower eyelids
* Brow lift
* Fat grafting
* Lip lift
* Laser resurfacing or chemical peel
Risks
* What are your complication rates?
* How often do you see:
* Hematomas
* Nerve injury **
* Infection
* Skin loss
* If a complication occurs, how is it handled?
* If I need a revision, what is your policy?
* Who closes and stitches ?
* What kind of stitches? Dissolvable?
Anesthesia
* Will I have general anesthesia or IV sedation?
* Who provides the anesthesia?
* Is surgery done in an accredited surgical center?
Cost
* What’s included in the quoted price?
* Are anesthesia, facility fees, garments, medications, and follow-up visits included?
* Are there any additional costs if surgery takes longer?
Picts of long term results?
“If I were your sister/family member what would you recommend I do—and what would you tell me not to do?”
Finally, ask the surgeon to point to a mirror and physically show you what the surgery can and cannot improve. Having them gently lift your skin to demonstrate the expected changes in your neck, jawline, and cheeks can give you a much clearer understanding of the likely outcome.
